                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No(s). 33693/2025
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 30-04-2024
in WA No. 1758/2021 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Madras]
THE SECRETARY, SCHOOL EDUCATION DEPARTMENT & ANR.  Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
K.SHANMUGAM                                        Respondent(s)
(IA No. 159284/2025 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN FILING)
 
Date : 22-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K.V. VISWANATHAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s) : 
                   Ms. Haripriya Padmanabhan, AAG
                   Mrs.Kanika Kalaiyarasan, AOR
                   Mr. Shourya Dasgupta, Adv.
                   Mr. Sabarish Subramanian, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
                   Mr. Vishal Sinha, Adv.
                   Mr. Bharathimohan M., Adv.
                   Ms. Preethi G, Adv.
                   Ms. V. Swetha, Adv.
                   Mr. Chandra Kiran K, Adv.
                   Mr. P. Ashok, Adv.
                   Mr. Vairawan A.S, AOR                   
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard Ms. Haripriya Padmanabhan, learned Additional
Advocate General (AAG) for the petitioners and Mr. Vishal
Sinha, learned counsel appearing for the respondent.
1

--- Page 216 ---
2. The  present  matter  calls  in  question  the
correctness of the order dated 30 th April, 2024 of the
Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at Madras
in WA No.1758 of 2021 which in turn has upheld the order
of the learned Single Judge. The learned Single Judge
allowed the Writ Petition of the respondent and directed
that S.No.99 of the provisional Selection List dated 20 th
November, 2019 will stand quashed and the State was
directed to proceed with the selection in line with the
observations made in the order of the learned Single
Judge.
3.  On 12th June, 2019, an advertisement was issued by
the Teachers Recruitment Board, inviting applications for
the post of Post Graduate Assistants.  The respondent
applied  for  the  post  of  Post  Graduate  Assistant
(Commerce) under the SCA (Scheduled Caste Arunthathiyar)
category.  The Notification at page 56 of the paper book
set out a total of 2144 vacancies with the following
break up:
(i) Shortfall vacancies    3
(ii) PWD vacancies  134
(iii)Backlog vacancies  336
      (iv) Current vacancies 1657
2

--- Page 217 ---
(v) Minority Language/   14
           Medium vacancies
4. Under the category of PWD vacancies, a separate
chart is set out at page 57 of the paper book.  Under
S.No.11 for the subject Commerce under category II among
four  vacancies  for  the  persons  with  benchmark
disabilities, one vacancy is reserved for SC-1 which
would  mean  Scheduled  Caste  category  -  one  vacancy.
Thereafter, the remaining part of the Notification deals
with the break up for other categories.  It transpires
that when the provisional list was published, only one
candidate  was  selected  under  the  SCA  (Tamil  Medium
Category) and the other seat was not filled up.  The
learned  Single  Judge  records  that  the  provisional
Selection  List  showed  that  the  candidate  was  not
available to fill up the selection which came to the turn
of SCA/HH i.e. Scheduled Caste Arunthathiyar/Hard of
Hearing.
5. Aggrieved,  the  respondent  moved  the  Writ  Court
contending that there was no reservation under the SCA
category for persons with disability and that the State
ought not to have considered the post as one coming under
the  category  of  persons  with  disabilities  and
consequently could not have carried forward the vacancy.
Learned  Single  Judge  accepted  the  contention  of  the
3

--- Page 218 ---
respondent and held as under:
“… The 2 nd respondent has misunderstood the
Notification and has come to a conclusion that
the 2nd candidate under SCA will fall within the
horizontal  reservation  of  persons  with
disability.  A careful look at the Notification
reveals the fact that the Commerce subject, there
is no reservation or selection turn for SCA HH
category.  What is provided under Category-II
under the persons with disability is only one
post for SC.  This has been wrongly construed to
mean that it falls within the SCA community.
This is an apparent mistake that was committed by
the 2nd respondent and the same is clear from the
letter dated 10.01.2020, which was sent to the
petitioner and which has been extracted supra.
The 2nd respondent completely misdirected itself
by considering the post to fall under Category-
II, of persons with disability and has proceeded
to hold that there was no candidate available and
this post has been carried forward to the next
recruitment.  This process adopted by the 2 nd
respondent is erroneous.  The Notification does
not  provide  for  horizontal  reservation  under
persons  with  disability  category  for  SCA
community in the subject of Commerce.  Therefore,
there was no need for the 2 nd respondent to
consider the post to fall within Category-II of
persons with disability.  The selection turn does
not fall under this category and it only falls
within the category of SCA (General)….”
6. This order of the learned Single Judge has been
4

--- Page 219 ---
upheld  by  the  Division  Bench  of  the  High  Court.
Aggrieved, the State is in appeal.
7. Learned AAG contends that under the roster at page
74 read with page 31 which is the statute setting out the
roster Entry 1266 (provided at page 31) would fall for
SCA Category II. The Court drew the attention of the

where the total vacancies have been compartmentalized.
The Court further drew the attention of the learned AAG

2. The  High  Court  of  Delhi  at  New  Delhi,  by  the  impugned
judgment  and  order  dated  7th May,  2026,  has  dismissed  the
appellant’s application for regular bail.
3. Appellant was arrested on 24th November, 2025, in connection
with FIR No. 24 of 2025 dated 5 th June, 2025, registered at Police
Station Shastri Park Metro, Delhi against six persons, under Sections
137(2), 143(4), 143(7), 61 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 and Section 81 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of
Children) Act, 2015. It is alleged that the appellant along with the
co-accused facilitated handing over a baby, newly born in a clinic, to
an issueless couple.

--- Page 221 ---
2
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and
perused the materials on record.
5. The  police  report  (charge-sheet)  has  been  filed  on  13th
February, 2026, but the charges have not yet been framed. The trial
is likely to take time to conclude since report from the Forensic
Science Laboratory is awaited.
6. It is also noticed that two women out of six co-accused have
been released on bail. Appellant is also a woman and entitled to the
benefit of Section 480 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Surakshya Sanhita,
2023.
7. T aking an overall view of the matter, we are of the considered
opinion that the appellant need not be detained in custody any
longer and that she could be admitted to an order for release on bail
pending trial.
8. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.
9. Needless  to  observe,  the  appellant  shall  not,  directly  or
indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any
person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such
facts to the court.
10. In the event there is any breach of the terms and conditions
for the grant of bail, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the
bail of the appellant.

--- Page 222 ---
3
11. It is also ordered that the  appellant shall diligently attend
proceedings  of  the  trial,  unless  exempted.  If  she  abstains  from
attending the proceedings without justifiable cause, that could also
be seen as a breach of the conditions for the grant of bail, and the
trial court will be free to pass appropriate orders.
12. We clarify that the observations made in this order and the
grant of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the
case.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION

          O R D E R
Leave granted.
2. Heard Mr. Viresh Kumar, learned counsel appearing
for the appellants and Mr. Ch Leela Sarveswar, learned
counsel  appearing for  respondent Nos.  2 and  3, the
brother-in-law of the first appellant and the estranged
wife of the first appellant.
3. The  present  appeal  calls  in  question  the
correctness of the order dated 13 th May, 2024 passed by
the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in Application
under  Section  482  No.16490  of  2020.   By  the  said
judgment,  the High  Court has  declined to  quash the
proceedings against the appellants in Case No.3378 of
2019 registered under Sections 498-A, 506 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 (for short, 'the IPC') and Sections 3/4
of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (for short, “the DP
Act”).
1

--- Page 226 ---
4. Learned counsel for the appellants has taken us
through the First Information Report (FIR) and the charge
sheet.
5. The  marriage  between  the  appellant  No.1  and
respondent No.3 was solemnized in 1998. FIR has been
filed on 2nd July, 2018.  A perusal of the FIR shows that
the case of the de-facto complainant is that five years
after the marriage in 1998, gauna ceremony was done and
thereafter respondent No.3 returned to her mother’s home.
It is alleged that the appellant No.1 avoided to take his
sister (respondent No.3) back into the matrimonial home,
started demanding “lot of money” because the father of
the respondent Nos.2 and 3 was a Subedar Major and
respondent No.2 was posted in Army Headquarters.  No
details  whatsoever  have  been  given  and  omnibus
allegations are made.  The time period during which the
demand was made and the nature of the demand have not
been set out.  Thereafter, certain facts are narrated as
to how the respondent No.2 took up the matter with the
District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police.  Here
again  no  particulars  are  given  as  to  when  those
correspondence were addressed.  An allegation is made in
the FIR that appellant No.1 had attributed mental illness
to  respondent  No.3  and  in  retaliation  the  de-facto
complainant  made  certain  allegations  against  the
2

--- Page 227 ---
appellants.
5. The charge sheet which has been filed also is very
vague.  We find that none of the ingredients of Sections
498-A, 506 IPC and Sections 3/4 of the DP Act are made
out.  The allegations are omnibus, stale and vague.
Allowing any prosecution to continue on the basis of
these allegations would be a complete abuse of process.
6. For the reasons stated above, we set aside the
impugned order dated 13 th May, 2024 of the High Court of
Judicature at Allahabad. Consequently, Case No.3378 of
2019 (arising out of FIR/Case Crime No.214 of 2018 dated
2nd July, 2018 registered at Police Station Shyamdeurwa,
District Maharajganj) pending in the Court of the Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Maharajganj and registered for the
offences  under  Sections  498-A,  506  of  the  IPC  and
Sections 3/4 of the DP Act shall stand quashed.
7. The appeal is allowed in the above terms.

K. DHINESH KUMAR                                   Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS

Date : 21-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.

 By Courts Motion
For Petitioner(s) 
                   
For Respondent(s)  Mr. Parijat Kishore, AOR
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This is a miscellaneous application in the form of a
letter written by the appellant in Civil Appeal No.500/2023
which  was  disposed  of  by  this  Court  vide  order  dated
24.01.2023.  This  Court  in  the  order  of  24.01.2023  while
allowing the appeal of the appellant K. Dhinesh Kumar , made
the following order:
“Leave granted. 
The parties entered into a matrimonial arrangement on
01.6.2006 and the marriage ceremonies were performed as
per Hindu rites and customs at Salem. It appears that
the marriage did not work out from the inception. In
fact the allegation of the appellant-husband is that
the marriage has not even been consummated. 
The strained relationship between the parties resulted

--- Page 231 ---
2
in the appellant filing a divorce petition on grounds
of cruelty under Section 13 (1) (i-a) of the Hindu
Marriage Act, 1955. The post trial divorce petition was
dismissed vide Order dated 11.12.2013 whereupon the
appellant preferred an appeal which has been dismissed
by the impugned judgment dated 10.1.2019. 
Notice was issued in the matter on 19.7.2019 recording
the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant
that what was now being sought was a decree of divorce
as the marriage had irrevocably broken down as the
parties had been living separately for 14 years. The
mediation endeavour in pursuance to that order has also
not produced any fruitful result. 
We put to learned counsel for parties that what was a
period of 14 years is now 16 years and the parties have
not lived together from the very inception of the
marriage. It is not a question of putting a blame on
one or the other but there can hardly be any doubt that
this is a case of irretrievable breakdown of marriage
and this Court is required to step in to exercise its
jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of
India.  We  are  fortified  in  our  view  by  the
pronouncement of judgment in 2021 SCC Online SC 702
titled “Sivasankaran Vs. Santhimeenal” dated 13.9.2021.
The  aforesaid  being  the  position,  we  endeavour  to
workout a solution for permanent alimony. Both the
parties are gainfully employed though the appellant is
earning more than the respondent. Some figures were
mentioned by both the sides but ultimately at the
suggestion of the Court it is agreed that an amount of
Rs.15,00,000/- be paid to the respondent as full and
final settlement of all her claims arising from the
matrimony. 
At the request of learned counsel for the appellant, a
period of three months is granted to make the payment.

--- Page 232 ---
3
In view of the permanent alimony being settled at the
willingness of the parties to go for a decree of
divorce, apart from the fact of irretrievable breakdown
of marriage, we are inclined to grant a decree of
divorce by exercising our jurisdiction under Article
142 of the Constitution of India. 
Sixteen years is too long a period of time for the
parties to stay apart and that too from the inception
of the marriage and it is the time for the parties to
go their separate ways to lead their lives on their own
terms. 
A decree of divorce be accordingly drawn up which would
however be released on the proof of payment of the
amount being filed in Court. 
The appeal is accordingly allowed leaving parties to
bear their own costs.”
2. In substance, this Court exercised its jurisdiction under
Article 142 of the Constitution of India and granted a decree
of divorce on account of the fact that for 16 long years, the
couple have been separated. By the said order, an amount of
Rs.15,00,000/- was fixed as the amount that the appellant
K.Dhinesh Kumar would pay to the respondent - J.G.Aruna.
3. In the present miscellaneous application the grievance of
the appellant is that the amount of Rs.15,00,000/- was first
sent to the respondent by virtue of a demand draft through
registered post at the residential address of the respondent.
That  registered  post  returned  back  with  the  endorsement
‘refused’. Thereafter the appellant filed a memo before the
Family Judge, Salem, Tamil Nadu (for short, ‘Trial Court’) on
05.04.2023 to record the factum of refusal by the respondent.

--- Page 233 ---
4
It is averred that the Trial Court sent a notice to both the
parties to appear before the Court. It is further stated that
the appellant appeared on 22.05.2023. The case was posted for
objection of the respondent on 03.06.2023.
4. The appellant submits that he filed a memo for bank
account details of the respondent so that he can deposit the
amount. It is stated in the letter that the respondent filed a
memo stating that the respondent is not willing to accept the
amount and the same was recorded by the Trial Court and the
memo was closed.
5. We further notice from the order sheet of the Trial Court
that the Trial Court has directed that since the matter was
disposed of by this Court, the petition is closed, granting
the appellant liberty to approach this Court to point out that
the respondent has failed to receive the amount and obey the
assurance given to this Court.
6. In this scenario, we direct that in the event of the
appellant, depositing the money before the Trial Court, the
appellant  would  be  deemed  to  have  complied  with  his
obligations under the order of 24.01.2023.
7. We  permit  the  appellant  to  deposit  the  amount  of
Rs.15,00,000/- before the Court of Special Judge for Family
Court, Salem, Tamil Nadu within a period of four weeks from
today.
8. On such deposit, the said Family Court shall keep the
said amount in a short term Fixed deposit in a Nationalized
Bank. The Family Court shall also intimate the respondent that

--- Page 234 ---
5
the amount is lying in deposit and it is up to her to withdraw
the amount. The Family Court shall give the respondent three
months’ time to withdraw the said amount.
9. A report may be sent to this Court, by the Family Court
concerned.
10. Post this matter on 02nd November, 2026 for compliance.

13772/2026. He sought bail in relation to

No.8/2026  dated  06.01.2026,  registered
with Police Station - Mandideep, District
– Raisen, Madhya Pradesh, for offences

of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
3. We find that the appellant, Pramod Kumar
   1

--- Page 246 ---
Arjariya,  has  been  in  custody  since
06.01.2026.

State of Madhya Pradesh, wherein it is
stated that the deceased-wife left the
company of the husband in June, 2025. She
admittedly  committed  suicide  on
05.12.2025. As matters stand, there is no
proof  of  any  contact  between  the
appellant and his deceased-wife during
that period. 
5. In such circumstances, we are of the
opinion that continued incarceration of
the appellant, Pramod Kumar Arjariya, is
not warranted at this stage.  It is for
the prosecution to prove its case during
the course of trial, but in the meanwhile
the appellant need not suffer further
incarceration. 
6. Accordingly, we accept the present appeal
and direct that the appellant, Pramod
Kumar Arjariya, shall be released on bail
in connection with the aforestated FIR on
such appropriate terms and conditions as
may be fixed by the trial Court.

appeal  is  allowed  in  the  aforestated
terms. 
9. We clarify that we have not made any
observations/comments on the merits of

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
ARBITRATION PETITION NO.21/2026
REVNOMIX SOLUTIONS LLP PETITIONER(S)
                              VERSUS
THE CONVO HOLDING LIMITED RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. This  petition  under  Section  11(5)  of  the
Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (Act), seeks
the appointment of a sole arbitrator to adjudicate
disputes arising from an Agreement dated 10.04.2023
(Agreement), executed between the Petitioner and the
Respondent to provide revenue management services to
the Respondent.
2. Briefly  observed,  the  Petitioner,  Revnomix
Solutions LLP, is a limited liability partnership
having its registered office in Mumbai. The Petitioner
is engaged in providing revenue management and data
analytics services to entities in the hospitality
industry.  The  Respondent-company,  is  a  company
1

--- Page 251 ---
incorporated  in  Cyprus  which  owns,  manages  and
operates  hotel  properties.  The  Respondent-company,
vide  the  Agreement  dated  10.04.2023,  initially
appointed the Petitioner to provide revenue management
services in respect of the Respondent’s three hotel
properties. Vide the first addendum dated 09.08.2023,
the Respondent engaged the Petitioner for a fourth
hotel in Italy. As per the terms of the Agreement, the
Respondent was required to pay consideration of a one-
time  setup  fee  of  €450  per  hotel,  and  monthly
commission calculated at 1.5% of Total Room Revenue,
payable in Euros upon the raising of monthly invoices.
Vide the second addendum, the monthly commission was
revised to 1.15% effective from 01.05.2024. 
3. It appears that a dispute arose when the Respondent
allegedly failed to make timely payment of monthly
invoices from around September 2023 onwards, despite
the Petitioner continuing to render services under the
Agreement.  Subsequently,  by  way  of  email  dated
25.07.2024, the Respondent terminated the Agreement,
which was accepted by the Petitioner. Thereafter, the
parties entered into discussions for settlement of
outstanding  dues.  The  Petitioner  asserts  that,
pursuant to such discussions, the Respondent  vide
communication dated 01.10.2024, agreed to pay 75% of
the  outstanding  amounts.  However,  although  this
2

--- Page 252 ---
proposal was accepted by the Petitioner, only part-
payments were sought to be made by the Respondent.
4. In these circumstances, the Petitioner, issued a
notice dated 17.10.2025 under Section 21 of the Act,
invoking arbitration and proposing the name of Ms.
Chandana Salgaonkar, Advocate as sole arbitrator. It
is stated that the Respondent failed to respond to the
notice within 30 days of receipt of the said notice.
Hence, the Petitioner has filed the instant Petition
under Section 11(5) of the Act.
5. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material placed on record.
6. Keeping  in  view  the  facts  and  circumstances
recorded above and the relevant provision(s) under the
agreement dated 10.04.2023, we deem it just and proper
to allow the instant Arbitration Petition and appoint
Mr. Ganesh Khemka, Advocate as the Sole Arbitrator to
resolve the disputes between the parties. In terms of
the  arbitration  agreement  as  well  as  subsequent
communication  between  the  parties,  the  seat  of
arbitration  shall  be  Mumbai,  India.  Ordered
accordingly. 
7. The Arbitrator shall have the liberty to fix his
own remuneration/fees.
3

--- Page 253 ---
8. Pending interlocutory applications, if any, also
stand disposed of.
..........................CJI.
(SURYA KANT)
............................J.
(JOYMALYA BAGCHI)
............................J.
(V. MOHANA)

1. Leave granted.

3. The appellant was charged for the
offences punishable under Sections 147,
148, 149, 302 and 307 of the Indian Penal
Code, 1860 arising out of Case Crime
No.131  of  2003  registered  at  Police
Station Kotwali, District Meerut, Uttar
Pradesh.  Upon conviction, the appellants
were sentenced to the death penalty by
the  trial  court.  A  reference  and  an
2

--- Page 262 ---
appeal preferred by the appellant were
made to the High Court of Judicature at
Allahabad vide Criminal Reference No. 21
of 2007, whereby the High Court, while
dismissing the criminal reference, partly
allowed the appeal of the appellant and
commuted  the  death  sentence  to  life
imprisonment.
4. On 16.04.2026, the following order
was passed in a connected matter being
S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 6745 of 2026:
“The issue for consideration in the
present petition is as to whether
the High Court has the jurisdiction
to  sentence  the  petitioner  to
imprisonment for life while fixing
a condition that remission could be
sought only after completion of 20
years of sentence.
Learned  Senior  counsel
appearing for the petitioner placed
reliance upon the judgment of this
Court in  Sukhdev Yadav  @ Pehalwan
v. State of (NCT of Delhi) & Ors. –
Criminal Appeal No.3271/2025 dated
3

--- Page 263 ---
29th July, 2025.
Learned counsel appearing for
the State submits that in any case,
the petitioner having completed 21
years of incarceration, his case
for  remission  is  under
consideration,  and  therefore,  a
period of four weeks may be
granted,  after  which  the  present
issue may be considered.
Considering  the  above,
particularly,  the  fact  that  the
petitioner has already completed 21
years of imprisonment, we direct
the  respondent  to  release  the
petitioner  forthwith,  until  and
unless he is required in any other
case, on such terms and conditions
as may be imposed by the concerned
Trial Court.
Ordered accordingly.
List the matter on
28.05.2026.”
5. In view of the above and taking into
consideration the fact that the appellant
has undergone incarceration for a period
of 22 years, and the fact that the co-
accused  have  also  been  released,  the
appellant  is  directed  to  be  released
4

--- Page 264 ---

in any other case, on such terms and

   UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. These  Special  Leave  Petitions  are  directed  against  the
Judgment and order dated 27.01.2022 passed by the Division Bench of
High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Bench at Gwalior, in Writ Appeal No.
69 of 2020, by which the order dated 13.12.2019 passed by the
learned Single Judge in Writ Petition No. 19912 of 2019 has been
modified and the writ appeal has been disposed of on the following
terms :-
“(i) For the reasons recorded in paragraph 17
(above), the tripartite agreement dt. 28.12.1997
is held to be illegal, affirming the finding of
the learned Single Judge in that behalf.  
(ii) The  agreement  dated  07.06.2019  between
Kamal Singh and G.D.A. is valid and binding upon
the parties.
(iii)  The impugned order dated 03.09.2019 is
upheld.
(iv)  The direction to the S.P.E. (Lokayukt) to
initiate proceedings and also register FIR is
hereby quashed.  However, the respondent/State
Government is directed to hold a detailed enquiry
to ascertain the role of officers involved in the
matter of execution of agreement dated 28.12.1997
and erring officer/s be dealt with in accordance
with law.
(v)   The  Registrar,  M.P.Cooperative  Societies
shall look into the affairs of the housing society
and under section 59 of the Abhiniyam of 1973 as
directed in para 24 of the order dt. 13.12.2019
passed in W.P.No. 19912/2019.”

--- Page 272 ---
3
2. We have heard learned senior counsel(s) appearing for the
parties at length.  In Para 17 of the impugned order, the Division
Bench has recorded the following prima facie findings with regard
to the Agreement dated 28.12.1997 :-
“17. Now, the second question that arises for
consideration is that of legality, validity and
enforceability of the agreement entered between
the petitioner society, GDA and owner of the
disputed land, Kamal Singh and other owners of
different parcels of the land described in
agreement dt.28.12.1997. The agreement is in
relation to 47 bigha and 3 biswa. 
This Court has perused the agreement and prima
facie has found that ; 
(i)  the  agreement  is  not  a  registered
agreement,
(ii)  there  is  no  resolution  of  the  GDA
authorising signatory i.e. CEO on behalf of the
GDA  for  execution  of  the  agreement
dt.28.12.1997.
(iii) There is no verification of the alleged
agreement by the owners/farmers of different
parcels of the land.
(iv) There is no document of ownership of
different  parcels  of  the  land  either  are
mentioned or made part of the agreement.
(v)  There  is  no  disclosure  of  payment  of
consideration to owners/farmers against handing
over of land to GDA.
(vi) No description of proportionate allotment
of plot to each of the farmers or owners under
the  formula  of  handing  over  25%  of  the
developed plots acquired through the agreement.

--- Page 273 ---
4
(vii) The society is not the owner or in
possession of any parcels of the land described
in the agreement, still it assured the right
and authority to negotiate with GDA in respect
of land described in the agreement.
As such, the agreement prima facie is
vulnerable on many counts and therefore can not
be said to be a lawful agreement. Chapter II of
the Indian Contract Act 1872 deals with the
contracts,  voidable  contracts  and  void
contracts.  Section  10  provides  that  all
agreements are contracts if they are made by
the free consent of the parties competent to
contract, for a lawful consideration with a
lawful object, and are not hereby expressly
declared to be void. 
As  such,  the  agreement  dt.28.12.1997,
prima facie does not fulfill the requirement of
the lawful agreement, as provided for under
Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act. It is
therefore, illegal contract within the meaning
of Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act.
Hence, not enforceable in law. “
3. It is pertinent to note that the appellant had challenged  the
order dated 28.08.2019 passed by the Gwalior Development Authority,
whereby  the  appellant  was  asked  to  pay  an  amount  of
Rs.1,68,24,000/- to the authority on account of the excess plot
area  of  21030  Sq.Ft.  The  appellant  had  also  challenged  the
validity  of  the  order  dated  03.09.2019,  whereby  the  Gwalior
Development Authority had allotted the plots to respondent no.4 in
compliance with the registered agreement dated 07.06.2019. Thus,
the issue with regard to validity of the agreement dated 28.12.1997

--- Page 274 ---
5
was not directly in issue before the High Court. Even otherwise, it
is trite law that the writ jurisdiction of the High Court under
Article 226 of the Constitution of India is summary in nature
wherein  a  detailed  inquiry  with  regard  to  facts  cannot  be
undertaken.  Presumably,  for  this  reason,  the  High  Court  has
recorded the  prima facie  findings with regard to the agreement
dated 28.12.1997. 
4. We, therefore, grant liberty to the petitioner to take recourse
to such remedy as may be available to it in law with regard to its
grievance in relation to agreement dated 28.12.1997 with incidental
prayers.
  
5. To the aforesaid extent impugned judgment and order dated
27.01.2022 passed by the Division Bench of the High Court is
modified. Accordingly, Special Leave Petitions are disposed of.
6.Pending interlocutory application(s), if any, is/are disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. The  High  Court  of  Madhya  Pradesh  at  Indore,  by  the
impugned  judgment  and  order  dated  25th November,  2025  has
rejected the appellant’s application for regular bail.
3. Appellant was arrested on 18 th January, 2025 in connection
with FIR No. 0111 of 2024 dated 24 th February, 2024 registered at
Police Station Sendhwa Gramin, District Badwani under Sections
406, 420 & 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and
perused the materials on record.
5. Though trial is in progress, it is likely to take time to conclude.
6. Having  regard  to  the  nature  of  accusation,  the  period  of

--- Page 296 ---
2
incarceration of the appellant and other attending factors, we are of
the  opinion  that  further  detention  of  the  appellant  in  custody,
pending trial, is not warranted and that he may be admitted to an
order for release on bail.
7. Accordingly, we set aside the impugned judgment and order.
8. Appellant shall be released on bail, subject to furnishing of
bail bonds to the satisfaction of the trial court and subject to such
other terms and conditions as may be imposed by it.
9. Needless  to  observe,  the  appellant  shall  not,  directly  or

person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such
facts to the court.

for grant of bail, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail
of the appellant.
11. It is also ordered that the appellant shall diligently attend
proceedings  of  the  trial,  unless  exempted.  If  he  abstains  from
attending the proceedings without justifiable cause, that could also
be seen as breach of the conditions for grant of bail and the trial
court will be free to pass appropriate orders.

of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.

--- Page 304 ---
2
owing to a statement of co-accused-Naveen, a Constable in the Police
Department.  A  marksheet  with  enrolment  no.  TGU/BSC/15081003

him to be admitted to an order for grant of bail in anticipation of
arrest.

aside.

indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any

3

the  investigating  officer  calls  upon  the  appellant  to  join  the
investigation, he shall do so by attending the police station.
12. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant of
bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
13. The appeal is allowed on the above terms.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

VENKATACHALAM & ANR.                        APPELLANTS
                          VERSUS
STATE OF TAMILNADU                          RESPONDENT
 
O R D E R 
1.   Leave granted.
2. By  the  impugned  judgment  and  order  dated  19th January,
2026, the Madurai Bench of the Madras High court has granted the
appellants’  prayer  for  bail  in  anticipation  of  arrest  inter  alia on
condition of payment of Rs.7,00,000/-.  
3. Appellants figure as accused in FIR No. 569 dated 24th October,
2025 registered with Police Station Kattuputhur, District- T richy. It is
alleged in the FIR that the appellants have committed offence(s)
punishable  under  Section(s)  316(2),  318(4)  and  351(2)  of  the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.
4. We have heard learned counsel appearing for the appellants
as well as the respondent-State.
5. The condition imposed by the High Court on the appellants to

--- Page 312 ---
2
make payment of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees seven lakh) as a condition
for grant of anticipatory bail is in the teeth of the decision of this
Court in  Ramesh Kumar vs. the State of NCT of Delhi 1 and,
hence, cannot be sustained.
6. Accordingly,  the  impugned  judgment  and  order  stands  set
aside.
7. It is directed that in the event of the appellants being arrested
in connection with proceedings arising out of the aforesaid FIR, they
shall be released on bail by the arresting/investigating officer/trial
without insisting on payment of Rs.7,00,000/- (Rupees seven lakh)
but on such other terms and conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
8. It is made clear that in the event the appellants breach any of
the terms and conditions imposed by it, the trial court shall be at
liberty to cancel the bail of the appellants.
9. Needless  to  observe,  the  appellants  shall  not,  directly  or
indirectly, by making inducement, threat or promise, dissuade any
person acquainted with the facts of the case from disclosing such
facts to any police officer or to the court.
10. We clarify that the observations made in this order and grant
of bail will not be treated as findings on the merits of the case.
11. The appeal is allowed on the above terms.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

TRANSFER PETITION (CIVIL) No.397/2025
PRAGYAN PADMAJA BEHARA          PETITIONER
VERSUS
JNANA PRAKASH RANA                         RESPONDENT
O R D E R
1. In course of hearing of this transfer petition, the petitioner-
wife  (Pragyan  Padmaja  Behara)  and  the  respondent-husband
(Jnana  Prakash  Rana)  were  referred  to  the  Supreme  Court
Mediation Centre.
2. The process of mediation has produced positive results.
The Mediator has sent a report that the parties have agreed to
resolve the inter se disputes and differences amicably. It has also
been  decided  by  them  to  apply  before  this  Court  seeking
dissolution of their marriage by mutual consent under Article 142
of the Constitution of India.
3. The parties have jointly filed an application under Article
142 of the Constitution of India in Court, which is taken on record.
The prayers in the application under Article 142 read as follows:
“(i)  Allow  the  present  Joint  Application  filed  by  the
parties under Article 142 of the Constitution of India
and grant the decree of divorce by mutual consent by
1

--- Page 316 ---
dissolving the marriage between the parties.
(ii)  Withdraw  to  this  Hon’ble  Court  all  the  cases
pending between the parties as detailed in para 2 of
the  settlement  agreement  dated  29.04.2026  and
quash/dispose off/close the cases.
(iii) Pass any other further order, which this Hon’ble
Court  may  deem  fit  and  proper  in  the  facts  and
circumstances of the case.”
4. During the course of the dispute, the parties filed various
cases against each other. Cases pending by and between
the parties before various courts are as under:
(a)  Maintenance  Petition  under  Section  144  of  the
BNSS,  2023,  being  CRP  No.  19/2025  filed  by  the
Petitioner–Wife,  pending  before  the  Family  Court,
Balasore, Odisha. 
(b) D.V. Case No. 66/2025 filed by the Petitioner–Wife,
pending before the Court of SDJM, Balasore, Odisha. 
(c)  Divorce  Petition  being  MC  No.  5859/2024  under
Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, filed
by the Respondent–Husband, pending before the Court
of  VI  Additional  Principal  Judge,  Family  Court,
Bengaluru.
5. We have interacted with the petitioner and the respondent
who  have  joined  the  proceedings  virtually  today.  They  have
separately submitted, while responding to our query, that they
have agreed to part ways without any threat,  force,  coercion or
undue  influence.  We  record  their  further  statement  that  the
mutual obligations as per the settlement dated 18 th May, 2026
have been worked out.
6. The parties having amicably resolved the inter se disputes
and differences, the terms of settlement contained in the joint
application shall form part of this order.
7. Accordingly,  in  exercise  of  power  conferred  on  us  by
2

--- Page 317 ---
Article 142 of the Constitution of India, we dissolve the marriage
between the parties by mutual consent by granting orders in
terms of prayer (i) of the joint application as well as prayer (ii)
thereof. Decree be drawn up, accordingly.
8. As a result of this order, nothing survives for decision on
the transfer petition. The transfer petition stands disposed of. 
9. The relevant courts/police stations shall mark closure of
the  cases/proceedings/complaints  that  are  pending/lodged
before it, once any party approaches it with a copy of this order.
10. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
11. We appreciate the efforts of the mediator in assisting the
parties to resolve their disputes amicably.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
Transfer Petition(Civil)  No.608/2025
NEHA KUMARI                                        Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
VISHAL THAKUR                                      Respondent(s)
                           O R D E R
1. The matter was taken up for hearing in the Committee Room.
Parties are personally present with their respective counsel.
2. We tried our best to convince the parties to save their
marriage. However, it appears that things have gone too far.
3. We are unable to persuade the parties further to have a
reconciliation.
4. In such circumstances, we allow this transfer petition as
prayed for. Accordingly, H.M.A. Petition No.395/2025 titled “Sh.
Vishal Thakur vs. Smt. Neha Kumari” filed by the Respondent
(husband) under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking
restitution  of  conjugal  rights,  pending  before  the  Court  of
Principal Judge, Family Courts, Muzaffarpur, Bihar is ordered to be
transferred to the Family Court, Karkardooma, East Delhi.
5. It is brought to our notice that the minor son, namely Archit,
for the first 3 years from the date of his birth was with his
mother i.e. the petitioner before us. Last year somehow, the
Respondent - father brought the minor son at his house, and since

--- Page 340 ---
2
then the minor son is residing with the father in Muzaffarpur,
State of Bihar.
6. Petitioner has many things to say as regards the mode and
manner in which the respondent took away the minor Archit. In this
regard, she has preferred GP No.12 of 2026, which is pending as on
date in the Court of the Principal Judge, Family Court East,
Karkardooma, Delhi.
7. We direct the Family Court to take up GP No.12 of 2026 for
hearing within a period of eight weeks from today and decide the
same on its own merits.
8. For any reason, if the Court is unable to pass any final order
on the application preferred by the petitioner before us i.e. the
mother,  then  the  Court  shall  at  least  provide  some  interim
arrangement as regards the custody of the minor son and dispose it
of within eight weeks from today.
9. Registry is directed to communicate this Order at the earliest
to the Family Court, Karkardooma, East Delhi.
10. We are informed that the next date fixed by the Family Court
is 26th September, 2026.
11. However, since we have passed this Order today, it shall be
open for the petitioner before us to produce this Order before the
Court concerned and get the date preponed. The Family Court shall
list the matter for hearing in the week commencing 29th July, 2026

--- Page 341 ---
3
12. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

(J.B. PARDIWALA)

ITEM NO.9               COURT NO.14               SECTION II-C
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) No. 7141/2025
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 18-12-2024
in WPMD No. 23982/2024 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Madras at Madurai]
S.SELVAKUMAR                                       Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
THE DIRECTOR GENERAL OF POLICE & ORS.              Respondent(s)
 
Date : 21-07-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
For Petitioner(s) : Dr. G. Sivabalamurugan, AOR
                    Mr. Selvaraj Mahendran, Adv.
                    Mr. Harikrishnan P V, Adv.
                                      
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sabarish Subramanian, AOR
Ms. Vrinda Bhandari, AOR
Ms. Nitya Jain, Adv.
                   
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard Dr. G. Sivabalamurugan, learned counsel for the
petitioner  and  Ms.  Vrinda  Bhandari,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State of Tamil Nadu.
2. Petitioner is aggrieved by order dated 18.12.2024, passed by
the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court (briefly the ‘High
Court’ hereinafter) rejecting the prayer of the petitioner to
preserve and produce the Call Details Report (CDR) of the concerned
mobile phones with covered location from 01.09.2022 to 30.09.2022.
1

--- Page 344 ---
3. Petitioner is an accused in Sessions Case No.56 of 2023,
prosecuted before the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Karur.
In the course of the trial, petitioner moved a Writ Petition
before the High Court making the aforesaid prayer. However, the
High Court rejected the request of the petitioner.
4. This Court by order dated 02.05.2025, issued notice and
directed the respondents to preserve the CDR for the aforesaid
period. In the proceedings before this Court on 25.07.2025, a
submission was made on behalf of the respondent-State that the CDR
for  the  aforesaid  period  would  not  be  relied  upon  by  the
prosecution. That apart, a submission was also made that the
Vodafone authority had informed the prosecution that the CDR could
only be preserved for a maximum period of two years.
5. Thereafter, on 26.08.2025, this Court directed the respondents
to file affidavit on the question as to whether the CDR details of
the concerned mobile numbers have been preserved or not. It was
stated that if those were no longer in existence, the Court should
also be informed as to when those records were deleted. Pursuant to
the aforesaid order dated 02.05.2025, State has filed counter
affidavit on 02.02.2026. Paragraphs 5, 6 and 7 of the said
affidavit read as:
“5. I submit that the above factual position
stands  independently  confirmed  by  Mr.  S.
Radhakrishnan, now Deputy Superintendent of
Police,  IUCAW-II,  Thanjavur  District,  who
earlier investigated Crime No.115 of 2022.
In  his  written  communication  to  the
Superintendent of Police, Karur District, he
has stated that while functioning as Circle
Inspector, K. Paramathi Police Station, the
2

--- Page 345 ---
investigation  was  handed  over  to  another
Investigating Officer on 13.09.2022, and that
during his phase of investigation, no Call
Detail Records were requested or collected in
respect  of witnesses  Periyasamy, Ponnusamy
and Mohanraj, or their mobile numbers. True
copy of letter 13.6.2025 is annexed herewith
as Annexure-R-1. (4-5)
6.  I  submit,  without  prejudice,  that  on
12.06.2025,  the  Inspector  of  Police,  K.
Paramathi Circle, Karur Rural Sub-Division,
addressed a letter to the Superintendent of
Police,  Karur  District,  requesting  Call
Detail  Records  relating  to  mobile  numbers
7639283925, 9003635299 and 9787960753 for the
period 01.09.2022 to 30.09.2022, solely for
the purpose of producing before this Hon'ble
Court. Therefore, request was sent to the
service  provider  for  call  details  of  the
aforementioned  numbers. However,  by e-mail
dated  13.06.2025.  the  service  provider
informed the Superintendent of Police, Karur
District, that the records sought exceeded
the  mandatory  two-year  retention  period
prescribed under telecom licence conditions,
and were therefore no longer available. Email
copy  dated  13.6.2025  received  from  the
service  provider  is  annexed  herewith  as
ANNEXURE-R-2. (6)
7.  I  submit  that  the  alleged  occurrence
pertains  to  September  2022,  and  the  writ
petition was filed after nearly two years,
with  full  knowledge  of  statutory  data-
retention limits. The present Special Leave
Petition  is  a  continuation  of  the  same
attempt and is clearly intended to delay the
Sessions Trial in S.C. No.56 of 2023, pending
before the Principal District Court, Karur.”
6. In the course of the hearing today, learned State Counsel
submits that the session’s case has ended in the conviction of the
petitioner under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC),
3

--- Page 346 ---
read with Section 120 thereof.  At this stage and more particularly
having regard to the fact that the request for preservation of the
CDR was made after completion of the two year period (incident had
occurred on 10.09.2022), there was no legal mandate for the
telephone company i.e., Vodafone to preserve the CDR. In any view
of the matter since the trial has concluded and petitioner has been
convicted, petitioner would be at liberty to raise all possible
grounds, including the present one, to assail his conviction and
sentence in the appeal that he may prefer. 
7. At this stage, we are not inclined to interfere in the matter.
8. Subject to what we have said above, the Special Leave Petition
is disposed of.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
 (IRAMNAZ)                                  (CHETNA BALOONI)
COURT MASTER (SH)                          COURT MASTER (NSH)
4

--- Page 347 ---

IN
C.A. NO. 6100/2024
[Arising out of impugned final judgment and order dated 17-03-2026
in C.A. No.6100/2024 passed by the Supreme Court of India]
UNITED INDIA INSURANCE CO.LTD.                     APPELLANT(S)/
                                                   APPLICANT
                                VERSUS
SAYONA COLORS PVT. LTD.                            RESPONDENT(S)
[PART-HEARD BY : HON. MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH AND HON. MR.
JUSTICE R. MAHADEVAN] 
 
Date : 21-07-2026 This matter was called for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE AHSANUDDIN AMANULLAH
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE R. MAHADEVAN
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. A.K.De, Adv.
                   Ms. Ananya De, Adv.
                   Mr. Chandrakanta Sahoo, Adv.
                   Mr. Pramit Saxena, AoR                   
                   
For Respondent(s) :Mr. Amit Anand Tiwari, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Anuj Chauhan, Adv.
                   Mr. Prashant, AoR
                   Mr. Surender, Adv.
                                      
                             O R D E R
We have heard learned counsel for the appellant and
learned Senior Counsel for the respondent.
2. We had allowed the main Civil Appeal No.6100/2024 vide
1

--- Page 348 ---
M.A. NO.2023/2026
our order dated 17.03.2026. However, we had kept the issue
of  fraud  being  committed  by  the  respondent  open  and
directed the Commissioner of Police, Ahmedabad, to submit
a report after setting up a Special Investigation Team.
3. Pursuant  thereto,  the  Commissioner  of  Police,
Ahmedabad, has submitted a report dated 30.06.2026. The
conclusion portion of the report reads as under:
"However, during the entire inquiry, the following
irregularities/criminal acts appear to have been
committed: 
(1) In the names of the employees of Sayona
Colours Pvt. Ltd., two proprietorship firms of
ELITE CHEMICALS, two proprietorship firms in the
name of RANGOLI ENTERPRISE, and proprietorship
firms in the names of JMB TRADERS and VISVAMEGH
AGENCY were created. The TIN/VAT/CST numbers of
these firms were generated after the fire. On the
basis of the purchase bills and purchase sheets
from these proprietorship firms, higher stock were
shown in Sayona Colours Pvt. Ltd., and on that
basis, the C.C. (Cash Credit) limit was increased
in the bank.
(2) It appears that no sale was made to Sayona
Colours Pvt. Ltd. by the two proprietorship firms
in the name of Shreeji Enterprises, IVA TRADEXCELL
PVT. LTD. and Nirav Chemical Industries and that
bills and affidavits were prepared without the
knowledge of the owners of the said companies.
2

--- Page 349 ---
M.A. NO.2023/2026
(3) It appears that Report No.FSL/Tapan/11/P/192
dated  13/09/2011  of  FSL,  Ahmedabad  City,  was
tampered with and produced before the Hon’ble
Court, thereby misleading the Hon’ble Court and
committing a criminal act.”
4. Having regard to the background/nature of the issue
and the material which has been gathered by the Police
during their investigation, we are satisfied that the
authorities/Police are required to follow up action in
terms of what has come during the investigation.
5. Accordingly, the matter stands finally disposed of
with a direction to the Commissioner of Police, Ahmedabad
to ensure that based on the report of the SIT as submitted
to this Court, appropriate action be taken in accordance
with law without any delay.
6. As the report has come, we find it equitable that a
copy of the same be handed over to learned Advocate on
Record for the respondent in Civil Appeal No.6100/2024.
Let the same be done by the Registry by tomorrow, i.e.,
22.07.2026. Thereafter, the same shall be resealed and
kept on record.
7. On an apprehension raised by learned Senior Counsel
for the respondent that the observations made in the order
dated 17.03.2026 in Civil Appeal No. 6100/2024 may cause
3

--- Page 350 ---
M.A. NO.2023/2026
prejudice to the respondent before Court/forum where the
follow up action is required to be taken by the Police
authorities, we indicate that the said proceedings should
be initiated on the basis of the report submitted to this
Court by the SIT and shall not be influenced by whatever
observations have been made by this Court in the aforesaid
order dated 17.03.2026.
8. Parties shall have liberty to canvass all points
available to them on facts as well as in law before the
concerned  Court/forum  and  the  said  Court/forum  shall
consider the same on their own merits, in accordance with
law.
9. The Miscellaneous Application stands disposed of in
the aforementioned terms. 
 (POOJA SHARMA)                                (ANJALI PANWAR)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We heard Mr. Shyam Divan and Mr. Navin Pahwa, the learned
senior counsel appearing for the petitioner and Mr. C.A.
Sundram and Dr. Donthi Reddy Venkat Reddy,  the learned senior
counsel appearing for the respondents.
2. In the impugned order passed by the High Court, more
particularly, in Paragraph 20 the High Court has observed
thus:-
“20. As per the proceeding sheet of the trial
Court, the matter was posted to 17.12.2025, for
orders in IA No.1748 of 2025 (Order VII Rule 10
CPC), and on 17.12.2025 the matter was adjourned
to 23.12.2025. According to the learned counsel
for the appellant, an application for extension
of the interim order was filed on 17.12.2025 by
way of abundant caution. If such an application
had indeed been filed on the previous day, the
necessity of filing another petition vide S.R.
No. 9050 of 2025 on 18.12.2025 does not arise.
Thus, there is no clarity as to whether any
valid  extension  of  the  interim  order  was
actually granted or not. Be that as it may, a
perusal of the proceedings sheet of the trial
2

--- Page 389 ---
SLP(C)  No.24442/2026
Court reveals that the matter had already been
transferred to the Commercial Court prior to the
filing  of  the  present  appeal.  In  such
circumstances, this Court is unable to call for
the  record  from  the  transferor  Court.
Furthermore, the material available on record
does  not  disclose  any  order  extending  the
temporary  injunction  beyond  15.12.2025.
Consequently, prima facie, the interim order of
temporary injunction ceased to operate after
15.12.2025.”
3. The plain reading of what has been taken note of by the
High Court is that there was nothing on record before the High
Court to indicate that the temporary injunction earlier granted
was extended beyond 15.12.2025.
4. However, the learned senior counsel appearing for the
petitioner brought to our notice the order passed by the XI
Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court at Hyderabad dated
15.12.2025 wherein there is a word “allowed” figuring in the
order with the signature.
5. According to the learned senior counsel appearing for the
petitioner this is indicative of the fact that the application
was allowed and the injunction was extended. However, on the
other hand,  the learned senior counsel appearing for the
3

--- Page 390 ---
SLP(C)  No.24442/2026
respondents would submit that in fact the application was not
allowed.
6. There is no clarity as regards the fact whether in fact
the application seeking extension was allowed or not.
7. In such circumstances, we remit the matter to the High
Court to look into this aspect. The High Court shall call for
the records and proceedings from the transferee court and get
an appropriate report from the transferor court in this regard.
8. The High Court shall hear both the sides and decide
afresh.  Let this entire exercise be undertaken at the earliest
and be completed, preferably, within a period of four weeks
from today.
9. We are further informed that application preferred by the
petitioner under Order XXXIX, Rules 1 and 2 of the Civil
Procedure Code, 1908, respectively is coming up for hearing on
04.08.2026.
10. Let the application under Order Order XXXIX be heard only
after appropriate clarification as regards the above. 
11. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands
disposed of.
12. Pending application(s), if any, stand disposed of.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NOS.2678-2679 /2025
       [@ SLP(C) NOS.12311-12312/2021)
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
BIMLA DEVI                                         Respondent(s)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. These appeals arise out of the judgment and orders passed by
the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at Chandigarh in Civil Writ
Petition No. 2596/2015 dated 10-09-2018 and CMA No. 2189/2020 dated
28-02-2020.
3. The High Court by the impugned order dated 10-09-2018 directed
as under:
“(6) The petitioner thus would be entitled to "minimum'
basic pay from the date she complete 20 years of
service till she was relieved on 31-7-2015 in terms of
para 22 of the cited judgement. Let such arrears be
paid to her within three months from the date of
receipt of certified copy of this order.
(7)  As  regards  to  the  petitioner's  claim  for
regularization of her service, no direction can be
issued, at this stage, except to observe that the
petitioner shall also be entitled to benefit in this
regard, if any. granted by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
the pending case.
(8) The writ petition stands disposed of in above
terms.”

--- Page 396 ---
2
4. It is evident from the impugned order that the directions were
issued in terms of the decision of the High Court of Punjab and
Haryana in  Union of India  Vs. Central Administrative Tribunal,
Chandigarh Bench and Ors.[Civil Writ Petition No.9167-CAT of 2007]
dated  02.03.2015.  The  relevant  portion  of  the  order  dated
02.03.2015 is as under:
“[22] We, thus, direct the petitioner-authorities to
re-visit the whole issue in its right perspective and
complete the exercise to re-formulate their policy and
take a decision to sanction the posts in phased manner
within a specified time schedule. Let such a decision
be taken within a period of six months from the date of
receiving a certified copy of this order.
[23]  Till  the  exercise  as  directed  above,  is
undertaken, the respondents shall continue in service
with their current status but those of them who have
completed 20 years as part time-daily wages, shall be
granted 'minimum' basic pay of Group 'D' post(s) w.e.f.
1.4.2015 and/or the date of completion of 20 years
contractual service, whichever is later".
5. Above quoted order passed in Union of India Vs. Central
Administrative Tribunal, Chandigarh Bench and Ors. was later set
aside by this Court by order dated 07.10.2021 in Union of India vs.
Ilmo Devi & Anr. [Civil Appeal Nos.5689-5690/2021]. The relevant
portion of the order is quoted hereunder:
“9. In view of the above and for the reasons stated
above, both the appeals succeed. The impugned judgment
and  order  passed  by  the  High  Court  and,  more
particularly, the directions contained in paragraphs 22
and 23 in the impugned judgment and order are hereby
quashed and set aside. However, it is observed that
quashing and setting aside the directions issued in

--- Page 397 ---
3
terms of paragraph 23 in the impugned judgment and
order shall not affect the case of the respondents and
they shall be entitled to the reliefs as per paragraph
23 of the impugned judgment and order passed by the
High Court.”
6. It is very clear from the above said direction that this Court
while quashing and set aside the directions in paragraphs 22 and
23,  had directed that the order shall not affect the case of the
respondents and that they shall be entitled to relief as per
paragraph 23 of the order extracted above (i.e. paragraph 4 of this
order).
7. In view of the above,  our direction will be that the
respondent will be entitled to a minimum basic pay of Group 'D'
post(s) w.e.f. 01.04.2015 and/or the date of completion of 20 years
contractual service, whichever is later.
8. With these clarification, the appeals are disposed of.

O R D E R
1. These petitions under Section 11(6) r/w Section 11(12)(a)
of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (Act), seek the
appointment  of  a  sole  arbitrator  to  adjudicate  disputes
arising  from  three  Freelance  Contracts  dated  17.10.2022,
17.01.2023 and 17.01.2024, executed between the Petitioner(s)
and the Respondent(s).
2. Since all three Freelance Contracts contain identical
clauses, reference shall, for the purposes of this Order, be
made to the contract executed on 17.10.2022.
3. Briefly observed, the Petitioner(s) is an Indian citizen
currently  residing  in  Germany  and  providing  consultancy
services,  in  product  and  business  requirements,  to  the
Respondent.  The  Respondent-company  is  incorporated  in
Delaware, USA and is involved in providing technology and
strategy services to the insurance industry. By way of the
three Freelance Contracts, the Respondent-company appointed
the Petitioner(s) to provide consultancy services in product
1

--- Page 400 ---
and business requirements.
4. It  appears  that  a  dispute  arose  in  2024  when  the
Petitioner(s) sought payment of EUR 48,141.69 [ approximately
Rs. 53+ Lakhs ], stated to be due to him under the three
Freelance Contracts. It is alleged that the Respondent neither
acceded to this request nor fulfilled its payment obligations
under the said contracts. The Petitioner(s) then resigned as
consultant with effect from 26.09.2024 and sought to initiate
arbitral proceedings in accordance with Clause 11.2 of the
Freelance Contracts.
5. Accordingly, vide communications dated 23.04.2025 to the
Respondent,  the  Petitioner(s)  suggested  the  name  of  two
advocates for appointment as the Sole Arbitrator to adjudicate
the dispute. However, the Respondent is said to have not
replied to this notice. Hence, the Petitioner(s) has filed the
instant Petition under Section 11(6) r/w Section 11(12)(a) of
the Act.
6. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the material placed on record.
7. Keeping in view the facts and circumstances recorded
above  and  the  relevant  provision(s)  under  the  Freelance
Contract(s), we deem it just and proper to allow the instant
Arbitration Petitions and appoint Ms. Iram Majid, Advocate and
Director, Indian Institute of Arbitration and Mediation, as
the Sole Arbitrator to resolve the disputes between the
parties. The seat and venue of arbitration, in terms of the

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We have heard Mr. K.M. Nataraj, learned Additional Solicitor
General. Referring to the affidavit filed on behalf of National
Investigation Agency (NIA), he submits that presence of NIA is not
necessary for adjudication of this case. Para 4 of the said
affidavit is extracted hereunder: 
“4.I submit that in the present petition, the
petitioners  have  called  into  question  the
order dated 13.06.2022 passed by the Hon’ble
High Court of Karnataka pertaining to the
investigation carried out by Old Hubali P.S.
in  connection  with  Crime  No.64/2022  to
74/2022.  I  submit  that  investigation
pertaining  to  Crime  No.64/2022  to  74/2022
have not been carried out by the respondent
No.6/NIA.  However,  the  petitioners  have
chosen to implead respondent No.6/NIA in the
above petitions even there being no specific
prayer sought for as against the respondent
No.6/NIA in the said matter.”
2. Having regard to the above, we recall that part of the order
dated  02.12.2022  granting  leave  to  implead  NIA  as  a  party

                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Petition(s) for Special Leave to Appeal (C)  No(s).  22197/2026
[Arising out of impugned judgment and order dated  06-03-2026 in
CAP(L) No. 40164/2025 passed by the High Court of Judicature at
Bombay]
HERITAGE LIFESTYLES & DEVELOPERS PVT. LTD.         Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
MADHUGIRI CO-OPERATIVE HOUSING SOCIETY LIMITED     Respondent(s)
IA No. 183241/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING C/C OF  I/JUDGMENT
 
Date : 21-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K.V. VISWANATHAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s) Mr. Guru Krishna Kumar, Sr.Adv.
Mr. Mohan M.Jayakar, Adv.
Mr. Nikhil Wable, Adv.
Mr. Bharat Bagla, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Heard  Mr.Guru  Krishna  Kumar,  learned  Senior  Counsel
assisting by Mr. Mohan M.Jayakar, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
2. The impugned order has refused to entertain the petition
filed under Section 37 of the Arbitration & Conciliation Act
1996  (for  short,  'A&C  Act').  Against  the  order  dated
10.11.2025 passed by the learned sole Arbitrator. The learned
Arbitrator had, by the order dated 10.11.2025, directed that
the Supplementary Development Agreement, which supplements the

--- Page 458 ---
2
original development agreement, be presented for stamping.
3. We find no good ground to interfere with the impugned
order on the facts of this case. 
4. At this stage, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner
submits that while even assuming the arbitrator was justified
in  impounding the  Supplementary Development  Agreement and
referring it to the stamp authority, various observations have
been made about the nature of the document.
5. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner apprehends that
these observations will come in the way of the Stamp Authority
deciding the issue under the Maharashtra Stamp Act, 1958(for
short, 'Stamp Act').
6. We are of the opinion that the apprehension is not
justified. Section 39 of the MS Act makes it abundantly clear
as to what course of action, the authority had under the Stamp
Act, is to employ in case a document is received by it under
Section 37(2) of the A&C Act. In the teeth of Section 39, it
is needless to observe that the concerned Stamp Authority will
decide the issue on its own merits uninfluenced by any of the
observations made by the Arbitrator.
7. Considering that the arbitration proceedings are held up,
the authority concerned under the Stamp Act, may act as
expeditiously as possible.
8. With these observations, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.

--- Page 459 ---
3
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.
(NIRMALA NEGI)                                  (MANOJ KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that though

in the main sequence where the deceased was beaten up, at

accused no.9 by the High Court of Gujarat vide order dated

that just because accused no.9 was not named in the

admittedly led to the death of the deceased, is sufficient
to indicate that the petitioner was there with a common
object of killing the deceased. Thus, it was submitted
that rightly the petitioner cannot take the benefit of the
bail granted to the accused no.9.

Diary No.35637/2026 1

--- Page 491 ---
2. The petitioner has been denied Regular Bail by the High
Court in connection with FIR No. 127 of 2023 dated
09.05.2023  registered  with  Police  Station  Sikariganj,
District  Gorakhpur  for  the  offence  punishable  under
Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, and 406 of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860 (for short “IPC”). The petitioner has
been in judicial custody since 30.01.2024.
3. The petitioner is accused of fraudulently posing himself
as  an  officer  of  a  well-known  company,  and  thereby
collecting a total amount of Rupees Seventy Lakhs from
the complainant, his neighbors, and his co-villagers,
promising  them  employment  and  power  charging  station
licenses.
4. A chargesheet has been filed in this case, in which it
has  been  recorded  that  the  petitioner  had  created
fraudulent e-mail IDs in the names of three persons whom
the petitioner had represented to be other officers in
the same company, to the complainant and others. These
three persons were named as accused in the FIR, but as
they did not exist, their names were dropped from the
chargesheet. 
5. The impugned order has been challenged by raising several
grounds such as the investigation being complete, absence
of recovery from the petitioner, as well as the ground
that out of the three accused who have been charge-
sheeted, only the petitioner has been arrested. 
Diary No.35637/2026 2

--- Page 492 ---
6. Despite the chargesheet being filed on 29.03.2024, the
jurisdictional court has not framed charges yet. The
investigation is admittedly over, and there is no reason
why the petitioner should be continued in jail, pending
trial.
 
7. On a prima facie consideration of the material on record,
we are of the opinion that the petitioner can be released
on bail, subject to cooperating with the investigation
and  such  other  terms  and  conditions  that  the
jurisdictional  court  may  deem  fit  to  impose.  The
petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer
(for short “I.O.”) as and when directed and shall also on
specific  directions  issued  appear  before  the
jurisdictional court. 
8. With the above directions, the Special Leave Petition is
disposed of.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed
of.

         UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioners have been denied anticipatory bail by the
High Court in connection with FIR No. 104 of 2023 dated
16.09.2023  registered  with  Police  Station  Dhurki,
District Garhwa for the offence punishable under Sections
120B, 420, 467, 468, 471, 472, 473, and 474 of the Indian
Penal Code (for short “IPC”). 
2. The petitioners are accused of entering into a criminal
conspiracy  with  the  co-accused,  by  which  the
complainant’s ancestral property was allegedly illegally
transferred to some of the accused who had created forged
sale deeds, on the basis of which the first petitioner –
in his capacity as a Revenue Karamchari – transferred the
said  ancestral  properties,  and  also  effected  online
mutations. The second petitioner – in his capacity as
Circle Inspector – is also accused of participating in
the said conspiracy. 
3. A chargesheet has been filed in this case, in which it is
recorded  that  the  investigation  found  that  multiple
online mutation orders were obtained from Circle Office,
Dhurki on the basis of the forged sale deeds. 
4. Notice was issued on 24.04.2026, when it was directed
that  no  coercive  steps  should  be  taken  against  the
petitioners,  in  addition  to  the  direction  to  the
petitioners to appear before the Investigating Officer
SLP(Crl.)  Nos.7224-7225/2026 2

--- Page 495 ---
(for short, “I.O.”) on 27.04.2026.
5. We heard the learned counsel for the petitioners as well
as  the  learned  Counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of
Jharkhand. 
6. The petitioners are revenue officers who are said to have
colluded with the other accused, and they are not working
in the offices where the offence is alleged to have been
committed.  Since  they  are  co-operating  with  the
investigation, we are of the opinion that they can be
released on anticipatory bail, on the condition that
whenever they are summoned, they shall appear before the
I.O. and shall co-operate with the investigation. 
7. We order that in the event of arrest of the petitioners
in connection with the offence enumerated above, they
shall be released on bail, subject to the terms and
conditions that the I.O. may deem fit to impose. 
8. Once the petitioners are released on bail by the I.O., on
directions issued by the I.O. or summons issued by the
jurisdictional court, the petitioners shall appear before
the trial court and furnish fresh bail bonds and ensure
due appearance in the trial.
9. With the aforesaid, these petitions stand disposed of. 
10.Pending applications, if any, also stands disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. By our order dated 13.05.2026, we had made ourselves
abundantly clear that the amount of Rs.15 lakh offered by the
husband is not reasonable.  We said so keeping in mind that
there is a minor daughter that the petitioner-mother has to
take care of.  The petitioner left her matrimonial home way
back in 2023. She has no other means of any income.  In such
circumstances, today we have made ourselves very clear to Mr.
Nishant Soni, who has joined the proceedings online that he has
to arrange for Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty five lakhs only)
towards full and final settlement.
2. We  give  one  last  opportunity  to  him  to  raise  the
necessary finance and make this payment to his wife and minor
daughter. 
3. Today, in the course of hearing, the learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner brought something very disturbing
to our notice. It appears that the petitioner has got herself
entangled in Section 138 NI Act complaints.  
4. We take notice of the fact that Criminal Case Nos.
5662/2025, 1387/2026 and 1097/2026 respectively are pending  in
the Court of 46-3rd Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional
2

--- Page 567 ---
T P(Civil)  No.3147/2024
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhuj, Kutch/1-Principal Senior Civil
Judge, Civil Court, Bhuj, Kutch/49 th-2nd Additional Civil Judge
and Chief Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bhuj, Kutch.  There
are in all three complaints lodged against her. The allegations
are  that  the  respondent  husband  is  responsible  for  this
proceedings against his own wife through one individual by name
Solanki Tulsi Rajesh.
5. We stay further proceedings of all the three criminal
cases including the non- bailable warrants issued by the courts
below.
6. On the next date of hearing, Solanki Tulsi Rajesh, the
original complainant of the three NI Act complaints, shall
appear before this Court through Video Conferencing.
7. Registry shall forward one copy of this order to the
Superintendent of Police, Bhuj, Kutch, who in turn shall inform
Solanki Tulsi Rajesh  of the order passed by this Court today
and further that she has to appear before this Court on
17.08.2026  through  Video Conferencing. 
8. List the matter on 17.08.2026.

The  appellant  stands  convicted  for  the

--- Page 595 ---
2
Penal Code, 1860 and has been sentenced to life
along with fine. On appeal, the High Court was
pleased  to  upheld  the  same.  Aggrieved,  the
appellant is before us.
We have heard the learned counsel appearing
for the parties.
The appellant seeks parity.
Inasmuch as it is not in dispute that the co-
accused has been granted suspension of sentence.
Further, taking into consideration the period of
incarceration already undergone by the appellant
and the appeal is of the year 2025, we are
inclined to suspend the sentence of the appellant,
during the pendency of the present appeal(s).
Accordingly, the sentence of the appellant is
suspended, during the pendency of the present
appeal(s), and he is granted bail on terms and
conditions to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
List the appeals in due course.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

been able to make any headway insofar as obtaining visa for Sandhya
is concerned. Ms. Bhati is still very hopeful that within next two

to take all steps for the purpose of stamping of his visa. We do
not know what Vinoth has done so far in this regard. There is no
affidavit filed by Vinoth as to what steps he has taken for the
purpose of stamping of his visa.

filed in the High Court at Calcutta in September, 2015

pending in the High Courts stood transferred to the
National Company Law Tribunal (for short, "the NCLT").

into force on 24th  March, 2020.  Learned counsel contends

further contends that for matters of this nature, the
threshold bar cannot apply retrospectively.

               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A

SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CIVIL) Diary No(s). 15842/2026
[Arising out of impugned judgment and order dated  27-01-2026 in
LPA No. 1147/2024 passed by the High Court of Punjab & Haryana at
Chandigarh]
KULDEEP KAUR                                       Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Respondent(s)
FOR ADMISSION , IA No. 201420/2026 - CONDONATION OF DELAY IN
REFILING /  CURING THE DEFECTS
 
Date : 24-07-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : 
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE K.V. VISWANATHAN
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN PALLI
For Petitioner(s)  Mr. Gurpreet Singh, Sr. Adv.
                   Mr. Noor Shergill, Adv.
                   Ms. Anuja Pethia, AOR
                   Mr. Rishabh Nigam, Adv.
                   Mr. Mansangat Singh Kohli, Adv.
                   Ms. Gunjan Nahata, Adv.
                   Mr. Aashish Paul, Adv.
For Respondent(s) 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. Heard Mr. Gurpreet Singh, learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner.
3. We agree with the reasoning of the High Court that the
case of the husband of the petitioner is covered by category
‘C’ of the CCS (Extraordinary Pension) Rules, 1939 (for short,
‘CCS Pension Rules’).
4. We would like to examine the question whether the High

--- Page 817 ---
2
Court was right in confining the relief to three years
preceding the date of filing of the writ petition. We are
conscious of the fact that the learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner-widow made a statement to this effect. However,
considering  the  fact  that  the  deceased  husband  of  the
petitioner made the supreme sacrifice of his life and he was
even awarded with the ‘Shaurya Chakra’, we are prima facie of
the opinion that the benefit should have been extended from
the date of death.
5. We are also prima facie of the opinion the Union of India
should have categorized the husband of the petitioner under
the correct category ‘C’ of the CCS Pension Rules and extended
the benefit, soon after his unforgotten demise.
6. These are not matters where the family or the widow
should be expected to go to Court to obtain relief. The fact
that they could go only after a long period of time should in
any event not come in the way of rendering justice to them.
7. Issue notice limited to this aspect, returnable on 05 th
August, 2026.
8. Let a copy of this petition be served upon the learned
Attorney General for India.
(NIRMALA NEGI)                                  (MANOJ KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        COURT MASTER (NSH)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. This special leave petition is reported to
be beyond time by 4368 days. 
2. The petitioner seeks to impugn judgment and
order passed by the High Court dated 06.03.2014
by  which  the  petitioner's  conviction  under
1

--- Page 973 ---
Sections 302 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 ("IPC") has been affirmed with a direction
that he shall not be entitled to any remission
and shall remain in jail till his death. 
3. The order of conviction finds support from
the testimony of witnesses including a child
witness (PW-1). 
4. In such circumstances, we do not find a good
ground to interfere with the conviction order.
However, we deem it appropriate to entertain
this petition on the limited question whether
High Court was justified in directing that the
petitioner's case for remission shall not be
considered  and  that  he  shall  suffer
incarceration till his death. 
5. Issue notice on the above limited aspect as
well as on the application for condonation of
delay, returnable in six weeks.

Mr. A.K. Sharma, Adv./AOR  
          UPON hearing the counsel, the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
We are not inclined to entertain this special leave petition
filed against an order of adjournment.  
However, we must take note of the fact that the petitioner has
been in custody since 07.09.2021 and his bail application, which
was filed on 08.12.2025, is awaiting consideration before the same
learned Judge since its very first listing on 09.01.2026.  We find
1

--- Page 1001 ---
that the learned Judge has now adjourned the matter to 21.08.2026
after calling for another status report. Status report dated
28.04.2026 was already before the learned Judge indicating that 12
out of the 19 listed witnesses had already been examined in the
course of the trial.  
As  the  petitioner  has  suffered  incarceration  for  a
sufficiently long period of time, he was entitled to have his bail
application considered on merits notwithstanding the rapid progress
or the lack thereof during the course of the trial.  
We, therefore, grant liberty to the petitioner to move an
appropriate application for advancing the hearing of the bail
application.  In the event of his doing so, the High Court is
requested to entertain the same and take up the bail application
for hearing and disposal as soon as possible.
The special leave petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ATUL S. CHANDURKAR
For Petitioner(s): Mr. Prativa Prakash Janapriya Nayak , AOR
  
For Respondent(s): 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Considering  the  reasons  mentioned  in  the  
Interlocutory Applications, delay in filing application 
for setting aside abatement is condoned.
2. Abatement is set aside.
3. Substitution application is allowed and the legal  
representatives of the petitioner are permitted to be  
brought on record.
4. Accordingly,  the  Interlocutory  Applications  
1

--- Page 1007 ---
bearing  Interlocutory  Application  No(s).161246/2026, 
161248/2026 and 161250/2026 are disposed of.
5. Delay in filing and refiling condoned.
6. Permission  to  file  Special  Leave  Petition  is 
granted.
7. We have heard learned counsel for the petitioner  
and have perused the orders of the courts below.
8. While we are not inclined to entertain the Special 
Leave Petition, we are, however, of the view that  
observations made by the High Court in Paragraph-18 of  
the impugned order dated 15.03.2024 is really not  
called for. When the High Court did not find merit in  
the Second Appeal, it should have simply dismissed the  
Second  Appeal.  There  was  no  reason  to  make  the  
observation that the property has escheated in favour  
of State of Punjab, more so when State of Punjab is not 
a party to the lis.
9. We, therefore, delete the observations made in  
Paragraph-18 of the impugned order dated 15.03.2024. In 
fact, Paragraph-18 in its entirety is set aside.
10. Subject to the above, the Special Leave Petition  
is disposed of.
11. Pending  application(s),  if  any,  shall  stand

         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SHEEL NAGU

For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Petitioner has been found guilty of “aggravated penetrative assault” and
sentenced to 20 years rigorous imprisonment.
2. Issue notice, limited to the point as to whether the petitioner was rightly
